messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: High error rate observed in euc1a ingress (5xx + conn resets). Automated alert triggered at 2026-03-15T09:07:14Z. Paging oncall @jamie (SRE).

jamie (sre): Acked. I'm on it. Initial metrics: 5xx rate ~18% across ALB -> envoy frontends, spikes correlate with AZ A euc1a.

priya (netops): Seeing a bunch of Envoy downstream conn reset logs from instances in euc1a-az-a, plus NLB healthy targets flapping. DNS TTLs still low (30s) but Route53 weight shifting shows oscillation.

jamie (sre): Can someone paste the Envoy stat lines? I want to confirm if it's connection resets or upstream RTTs.

priya (netops): Pasted snippets from the edge:```
[2026-03-15T09:05:48Z] envoy downstream_reset: 523 resets/sec, ECONNRESET
[2026-03-15T09:06:01Z] nlb-target-health: target euc1a-az-a i-0abc123 unhealthy, healthcheck 5xx
[2026-03-15T09:06:30Z] route53: weighted routing drift detected between euc1a/euc2
```

jamie (sre): That matches what I'm seeing in the dashboard. Error rate jump + Envoy reset counter spike started ~09:05Z. Impact surface: hosted api endpoints -> short tail latency increase for streaming and a subset of requests failing with 502/504. Estimating ~14% of production traffic affected in euc1a.

neil (sre): I'm grabbing node-level metrics. Are we sure it's not a kernel-level conntrack exhaustion? Kernel logs from euc1a-az-a show lots of TIME_WAIT accumulation but not full exhaustion.

priya (netops): Not conntrack. We're seeing MESG: "connection reset by peer" on the NLB->node path. Also noticed a simultaneous control-plane health update from the cloud provider for AZ A — they reported a transient network fabric degradation in that AZ 3 minutes ago.

product-ops: @jamie can we get a quick customer impact note to CS? Emma?

emma (cs): Customers A, C have small uptick in 5xx reports. I'll flag priority customers and open a ticket. ETA initial impact summary in 10m.

jamie (sre): Mitigation plan: 1) Shift traffic away from euc1a to euc2/euc3 by updating Route53 weights and route priority. 2) Temporarily increase ALB healthcheck thresholds to avoid flapping. 3) If healthy, spin up standby instances in euc1b and rebalance. 4) If DNS weight shift doesn't stabilize quickly, consider region-level failover for critical routes. Starting step 1 now.

priya (netops): I'm initiating Route53 weight shift: set euc1a -> 20%, euc2 -> 50%, euc3 -> 30%. TTL is 30s so changes should propagate in ~30-60s.

deploy-bot: Route53 weights updated by priya at 2026-03-15T09:09:52Z.

jamie (sre): Observing immediate drop in errors to ~8% after weight change. Envoy reset rate down to ~180/sec (from 523). Good. Holding to confirm stability for 5m.

neil (sre): I've also disabled autoscaling group AZ affinity for euc1a to allow replacement nodes to land in euc1b while we keep the control-plane actions minimal. Spawning two replacement instances now.

priya (netops): ALB target group healthcheck threshold bumped to healthy threshold=3 failure threshold=6 to reduce noisy flapping. Applied.

jamie (sre): Quick note: Logs show a pattern where TCP handshake succeeds then upstream resets during TLS record read. Could be intermittent hardware-level NIC reset or provider fabric.

router-watch: Noted BGP updates from the provider around the same window — some routes were briefly withdrawn for euc1a-az-a. Correlation looks strong.

emma (cs): Customer comms: We sent a brief status to impacted customers (P1s) noting elevated error rates and active mitigation. No data loss reported.

product-ops: Any impact on Dedicated/reserved instances customers?

jamie (sre): Dedicated customers with endpoints pinned to euc1a may see degraded performance. For those customers we are offering immediate failover help. Priya, can we list pinned accounts?

priya (netops): Listing pinned endpoints now. Two enterprise customers with pinned euc1a endpoints — reaching out to their SEs.

neil (sre): Replacement instances are up in euc1b, load balancing healthy. Error rate ticked down to 2-3% across the cluster.

jamie (sre): I'm going to start the oncall handoff to neil for mitigation verification and postmortem. Leaving the incident channel for tracking. Primary action items for postmortem: precise timeline of provider fabric event, Route53 weight decision rationale + timestamp, why ALB targets flapped, and cleanup plan for pinned customers.

neil (sre): Taking over. I'll keep the channel updated and coordinate with netops for provider ticket. Priya, can you open a provider support case with the fabric logs and request incident reference?

priya (netops): Case opened: REF-20260315-1108 with provider. Sent logs and asked for hardware NIC behaviour analysis.

jamie (sre): Thanks all. Handing off to neil. Incident severity: SEV2 (partial regional outage). Root cause suspected: provider AZ fabric instability causing NLB <-> instance resets leading to Envoy connection resets and ALB target flapping.

emma (cs): Final note for customers: we'll follow up with a postmortem once we have provider confirmation. For now, impact reduced and traffic restored.

neil (sre): Will keep monitoring for 30m then mark mitigated. Closing pager but keeping channel open for follow-ups.

incident-bot: Incident mitigated at 2026-03-15T09:50:00Z. Severity de-escalated to monitoring.
